review_notes: Read the whole file. I searched Mathlib for a matrix symmetrization (none; only unrelated SetRel.symmetrize), for matrix quadratic form structures (Matrix.toQuadraticForm' exists, but the file only has lemmas about `x ⬝ᵥ M *ᵥ x`, not a competing definition), and for bilinear form matrices (formMatrix is a named specialisation on continuous bilinear maps, so I treated it as acceptable). The one concrete finding is `openCube`, which is the sup-norm ball of radius π. The evidence is Main.lean's hand-proved `isOpen_openCube`. The case is moderate: the definition is tiny and the cost is a few extra lines. I did not verify the exact Mathlib lemma names for the replacement proof (e.g. `pi_norm_lt_iff'`) beyond reading its statement.

findings.excerpt: def openCube (N : ℕ) : Set (Fin N → ℝ) := {x | ∀ j, |x j| < Real.pi}
findings.problem: `openCube N` is the open ball of radius π about 0 for the sup norm on `Fin N → ℝ`, i.e. `Metric.ball 0 Real.pi`. Mathlib already has `pi_norm_lt_iff'` (for `0 < r`, ‖x‖ < r ↔ ∀ i, ‖x i‖ < r), and the case N = 0 agrees. The file introduces a separate set with no API. As a result Main.lean has to re-prove openness by hand with an `iInter` argument, instead of using `Metric.isOpen_ball`. Membership and injectivity-on-cube statements also cannot use ball lemmas.
findings.proposed_change: Define it as an abbreviation or notation for the ball, e.g. `abbrev openCube (N : ℕ) : Set (Fin N → ℝ) := Metric.ball 0 Real.pi`, and prove a single membership lemma `x ∈ openCube N ↔ ∀ j, |x j| < Real.pi` via `mem_ball_zero_iff` and `pi_norm_lt_iff'` (`Real.pi_pos`). Keep the name `openCube` for readability. `isOpen_openCube` then becomes `Metric.isOpen_ball`.
findings.benefit: Removes a competing notion of the cube. Openness and other ball facts come directly from Mathlib. The hand-written `isOpen_openCube` proof in Main.lean is no longer needed. Readers see that this is the standard sup-norm ball.

evidence.excerpt: have h : openCube N = ⋂ j : Fin N, {x : Fin N → ℝ | |x j| < Real.pi} := by
lemma pi_norm_lt_iff' (hr : 0 < r) : ‖x‖ < r ↔ ∀ i, ‖x i‖ < r := by
